sources.publisher: Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale (MRAe) Hauts-de-France, IGEDD; published on the Ministère de la Transition écologique, portail de l'évaluation environnementale
sources.summary: The regional environmental authority's opinion, adopted at its session of 11 August 2026, concerns the project by LLE01 SNC to convert about 23 ha of industrial wasteland (the former Stora Enso site, used since the 1930s for a sugar works and then a paper mill, closed in 2021 and demolished in 2022) at rue de la Papeterie in Brebières and rue de Brebières in Corbehem into a campus of four data-centre buildings (A, B, C and D) with an electrical substation, a waste-heat recovery building and two gatehouses, about 10 ha of building footprint and buildings about 30 m high. It gives 264 MW of IT power (60 MW IT for each of A and B, 72 MW IT for each of C and D) and 212 emergency generators (1,250 MW thermal) under ICPE rubriques 3110 and 1436; the grid connection requires a new 225 kV substation at Noyelles-sous-Bellonne (parcel ZC 151) and about 4 km of underground lines by RTE. The authority was referred the file on 25 June 2026 by Brebières for the building-permit application on that commune, on 30 June 2026 by the Osartis-Marquion community of communes for the Corbehem building permit, and on 28 July 2026 by the DREAL for the environmental-authorisation application. The first building is forecast to operate in early 2030 with phased build-out to 2036; these are forecasts and are not used.

sources.summary: The regional environmental authority's delegated opinion of 3 September 2026 concerns the construction of data centre PAR03 by SNC DATA SERRES at Ballainvilliers (Essonne), referred by the Préfet de l'Essonne and the Paris-Saclay agglomeration community within an environmental-authorisation and building-permit procedure (impact study dated 4 December 2025). The project redevelops a 61,069 m2 former industrial site with about 30,000 m2 of logistics buildings, operated by MDS until July 2025 and to be demolished, bounded to the east and south-east by the RD186; 3,978 m2 is to be transferred to the commune. It comprises one building of three blocks on three levels with six data halls of 12 MW IT each (72 MW IT), 19,324 m2 of floor area, a substation, a waste-heat building, 44 emergency generators (341.34 MW) and 84 rooftop chillers, with 116.9 MW of electrical demand at full load by 2039 and a double 225 kV underground connection to RTE's Escargot substation about 9 km away. Construction is scheduled in phases between 2027 and 2032 (forecast, not used).

sources.title: Loudoun County LOLA land-development applications named Sterling Technology Park (site plan EPLAN-2025-0027; performance bond PBOND-2026-0163)
sources.summary: The county's land-development applications layer returns three records named Sterling Technology Park, all on one polygon (one ring, 29 vertices, 12.27 geodesic acres, about 400 by 232 m) that equals the whole county parcel 033453879000; its planar centroid (-77.4292182, 38.9959385) lies inside it. Engineering Plan EPLAN-2025-0027 (application 12 February 2025, status In Review) and performance bond PBOND-2026-0163 (application 21 October 2026, In Review) are both described as '(Conditional Approval) Sterling Technology Park - Proposed Construction of Data Center Building ,Mechanical Yards, Guard Booth, and related infrastructure' [sic]; plat PLAT-2026-0100 (8 July 2026, In Review) is the 'Dedication of Right of Way an [sic] Easements Associated with EPLAN-2025-0027'.
sources.date_semantics: The status observation is the PlanApplicationDate of performance bond PBOND-2026-0163 (2026-10-21T11:58:39Z, 07:58 Eastern daylight time on 21 October 2026; the layer's date fields are Eastern time with daylight saving): the county's record that a performance bond for the conditionally approved data center site plan EPLAN-2025-0027 was submitted. It is not an approval or a building permit: the plan remains In Review with conditional approval, so no consent in effect and no physical work are asserted. The July 2026 plat is earlier than the admission window and is context only. The layer carries no record-version timestamp; published_at is the capture date (27 October 2026 UTC), the date on which this record version was observed being served by the county. The record's number sits in sequence with neighbouring 2026 bond and plat numbers of the same or adjacent days (see the 2026 sequence capture), which supports the recorded date as its submission date.

sources.summary: The layer holds 80 PBOND-2026 and 147 PLAT-2026 records. Plat numbers rise with their application dates without exception (PLAT-2026-0001 on 6 January to PLAT-2026-0160 on 23 October 2026); bond numbers mostly rise with their dates (PBOND-2026-0002 on 15 January to PBOND-2026-0174 on 23 October 2026), with seven adjacent inversions in which a later-numbered bond carries an earlier date (the largest is PBOND-2026-0137, dated 18 May 2026, after PBOND-2026-0135 of 19 August), so a bond's date can precede the assignment of its number. The bonds relied on sit in sequence with their neighbours: PBOND-2026-0121 to 0124 on 7 August, between PBOND-2026-0120 (4 August) and 0125 (10 August); PBOND-2026-0150 and 0151 on 5 October, between 0149 (30 September) and 0152 (9 October); PBOND-2026-0163 on 21 October, between 0162 (19 October) and 0164 (21 October). PLAT-2026-0121 on 12 August sits between 0120 (9 August) and 0122 (12 August). The newest bond and plat applications are dated 23 October 2026.
